decisions.reason: The filler-image rule does not change the requirement to create the magazine template; the same message only confirms that template creation is complete.
Adding subject-relevant filler images to pages with white space does not alter author names, author-photo identity, source, or placement.
The client selects additional images as the white-space correction without changing the confirmed Inter font family or its thicker treatment.
The filler-image decision does not affect flipbook platform or branding state; the independent white-label request in the same message is already represented by a matching MODIFY.
The requested filler images are article-subject imagery and do not change the required shape or size of author photos.
Adding images to fill white space does not change the existing two-page spread behavior or even-page-count constraint.
The filler-image quantity and relevance rules do not modify article category labels, mappings, sources, style, or placement.
The white-space correction does not change the restriction against red in the Dorian Vale article or the reservation of red for the cover.
The image additions do not change which cover-mentioned articles must be included, their designer-determined placement, or their exclusion from the Flat Plan.
The filler-image rule does not alter inclusion or end-of-magazine placement of the supplied tribute page.

The issue-assembly requirement already includes images as content inputs; the new quantity and subject-relevance constraints belong to the separate atomic article-ending requirement and should not be duplicated here.

Although image additions may affect pagination during layout, the table of contents still uses final page numbers after pagination is finalized, so its current requirement state remains valid unchanged.
